subject.title: [Bug]: ACPX update expands to 2.1 GiB; OOM leaves core/plugin drift that startup does not repair

question: Should interrupted official-plugin convergence resume automatically from a persisted update transaction before gateway startup, or should the updater roll core back when plugin convergence cannot complete?
rationale: Both approaches can restore a runnable core/plugin combination, but they establish different network, pin-preservation, package-manager rollback, and startup-readiness contracts that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Resume Interrupted Convergence
options.body: Persist the intended channel and official-plugin targets before core replacement, then resume only that interrupted transaction before loading plugins.

options.title: Rollback Core On Failure
options.body: Treat core and official plugins as one update unit and restore the previous core when convergence cannot finish.

options.title: Require Explicit Repair
options.body: Keep startup network-free but provide a visible in-product Fix action and refuse stale official plugins with actionable recovery state.

recommendation.title: Resume Interrupted Convergence
recommendation.body: Persist the intended channel and official-plugin targets before core replacement, then resume only that interrupted transaction before loading plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans the existing official synchronization contract and managed-plugin recovery paths needed for this choice.
